skill.name: starknet-identity
skill.description: Register AI agents on-chain using the ERC-8004 Trustless Agents standard. Manage agent identity as NFTs, build reputation through feedback, and request third-party validation.
skill.summary: Manage Starknet agent identity, reputation, validation, and A2A discovery through ERC-8004 registries.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are markdown syntax, documentation links, placeholders, or expected configuration examples. The raw private-key signer example is confirmed because it grants transaction authority. Semantic review also found funded on-chain writes, unpinned installation, and transferable reputation risks.

remediation.issue: The example constructs an account with a raw private key.
remediation.suggestion: Use a wallet connector, hardware signer, or documented secret manager. Never print, persist, or request private keys in prompts.

remediation.issue: Examples can submit transactions from a funded Starknet account.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before every write. Display network, contract address, entrypoint, calldata summary, fees, and signer before submission.

remediation.issue: The prerequisite installs the latest available starknet package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and lockfile. Verify package provenance before installation or updates.

remediation.issue: Transferred identity NFTs retain reputation from prior ownership.
remediation.suggestion: Show ownership history and separate current-owner trust from historical agent reputation after transfers.

semantic_findings.title: Funded Wallet Transactions Require Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to submit registry, feedback, and validation transactions from a funded account. Incorrect addresses or calldata can spend fees and create irreversible state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly call account execution methods after requiring a funded account. These are direct on-chain writes with financial and state-change impact.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Installation
semantic_findings.description: The prerequisite installs starknet without a version constraint. A future compromised or incompatible release could enter the user's environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is exactly npm install starknet with no version or lockfile guidance. The supply-chain exposure is direct and clearly evidenced.

semantic_findings.title: Transferred Identity Inherits Historical Reputation
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that a transferred identity NFT keeps its reputation. A new controller could benefit from trust earned by the previous owner.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 305 explicitly says the new owner inherits reputation. This creates a clear ownership-transition trust risk for reputation consumers.

content.user_title: Manage Starknet Agent Identity with ERC-8004
content.value_statement: AI agents need verifiable identity and trust signals across services. This skill guides ERC-8004 registration, reputation, validation, and A2A discovery on Starknet.
actual_capabilities: Registers an AI agent in an ERC-8004 identity registry with metadata and a token URI.
Queries agent existence, ownership, metadata, and total registry counts.
Updates owner-controlled agent metadata through Starknet contract calls.
Creates authorized feedback flows and reads reputation summaries or individual entries.
Requests validator assessments, submits responses, and queries validation status.
Maps Starknet identity details into an A2A Agent Card for discovery.
limitations: Requires deployed ERC-8004 registry addresses, compatible ABIs, an RPC endpoint, and a funded Starknet account.
Provides implementation examples, not audited contracts or deployment automation.
Does not verify third-party validator quality or guarantee reputation accuracy.
On-chain writes can incur fees and cannot always be reversed.

use_cases.title: Launch a Verifiable Agent
use_cases.description: Register an agent, publish core metadata, and connect its on-chain identity to an A2A discovery card.

use_cases.title: Add Reputation to a Marketplace
use_cases.description: Implement authorized client feedback and display count, score, tags, revocation state, and ownership context.

use_cases.title: Operate an Agent Validator
use_cases.description: Receive validation requests, submit scored responses, and expose validation summaries for downstream trust decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Agent Registration
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Starknet ERC-8004 registration plan for [agent]. Include required metadata, registry inputs, signer checks, and confirmation before any transaction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new agent identity

prompt_templates.title: Read Agent Trust Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Query agent [agent_id] on registry [address]. Summarize ownership, metadata, feedback count, average score, and validation results without changing chain state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Read-only inspection of an existing agent

prompt_templates.title: Implement Authorized Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the ERC-8004 feedback flow for agent [agent_id]. Validate owner authorization, chain ID, expiry, signer, score range, and replay protection.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complete Identity Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ERC-8004 integration for [service]. Cover registration, metadata updates, A2A discovery, reputation, validation, ownership transfers, failures, and explicit transaction approvals.

output_examples.input: Plan registration for a data analysis agent on Starknet testnet.
output: Prepared identity metadata for name, type, version, model, and status.
Listed the registry address, token URI, signer, balance, network, and ABI checks.
Added an approval checkpoint before submitting the registration transaction.

output_examples.input: Summarize trust data for agent 42 without writing to the chain.
output_examples.output: Agent 42 exists and has a recorded owner. The report includes metadata, feedback totals, average score, validators, and ownership-transfer context.

output_examples.input: Review a feedback authorization before submission.
output: Confirmed the agent identifier, client address, chain identifier, registry address, signer, entry limit, and expiry.
Flagged expired signatures, owner changes, self-feedback, invalid scores, and reused authorization data.

best_practices: Confirm the Starknet network, registry address, signer, calldata summary, and estimated fees before every write.
Use a wallet connector or protected signer instead of placing raw private keys in prompts, source files, or logs.
Show ownership history when presenting reputation because identity transfers preserve historical trust data.
anti_patterns: Do not submit transactions automatically after generating example calldata.
Do not trust reputation scores without checking feedback sources, revocations, tags, validators, and current ownership.
Do not install unpinned dependencies or use unknown registry addresses.

faq.question: What does ERC-8004 provide?
faq.answer: It defines identity, reputation, and validation registries for AI agents. This skill applies those workflows to Starknet.

faq.question: Does the skill deploy ERC-8004 contracts?
faq.answer: No. It expects compatible registries and ABIs to exist. Contract authoring, auditing, and deployment require separate tools.

faq.question: Can I use the skill for read-only queries?
faq.answer: Yes. Identity, reputation, and validation query examples use a provider and do not require a transaction signer.

faq.question: Does the skill need a private key?
faq.answer: Writes require an authorized signer. Use a wallet connector, hardware signer, or secret manager instead of exposing a raw private key.

faq.question: How does feedback authorization work?
faq.answer: The owner signs scoped data containing the agent, client, limits, expiry, chain, registry, and signer. The client submits it with feedback.

faq.question: What happens when the identity NFT is transferred?
faq.answer: The new owner controls future updates, while historical reputation remains attached. Applications should display ownership changes when evaluating trust.
